# cutver 0.20.0 — 2026-11-20

This release turns the release itself into a contract. Three new surfaces make the pipeline inspectable
instead of narrated: `cutver plan` says what a release will do without doing it, `cutver attest` records
a gate's verdict so `publish` can refuse a claim nobody verified, and the CI channel writes what the
workflow used to parse out of a log. Alongside them, every JSON surface now carries a `schemaVersion`.

Two of those changes are visible to a consumer that parses cutver's output. They are at the top, with
what to change.

## Breaking changes

**Every JSON object opens with `schemaVersion: 1`** ([#327](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/327)).
This covers `bump --json`, `bump --report`, `changelog latest --json`, `changelog show --json`,
`plugin list --json`, `plugin info --json` and `plugin search --json`. The rule for version 1 is
additive: keys only get added, so a consumer that ignores unknown keys keeps reading the same values.
The one shape change is `plugin search --json`, which used to print a bare array — an array has nowhere
to put a version, so it now emits `{"schemaVersion": 1, "plugins": [...]}` and callers read
`.plugins[]` instead of `.[]`.

*To migrate*: read `schemaVersion` first and branch on a value you were not written for. Only
`plugin search --json` needs a parser change for version 1: `.plugins[]` instead of `.[]`.

**A failure under machine output is one JSON object on stderr**
([#328](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/328)). When the invocation asked for machine output —
`--json`, plus `--report` for `bump` — a failure is now exactly this, on one line:

```json
{"schemaVersion":1,"error":{"code":"config","exitCode":1,"message":"…"}}
```

*To migrate*: stop grepping the human sentence. The class is `.error.code` (a stable string), the exit
status is unchanged, and `.error.message` carries the text you were matching before.

## `cutver plan`: the release as data, and nothing else
[#329](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/329)

`cutver plan [--json]` computes the release the workspace is about to cut and changes nothing: no write,
no stage/commit/tag/push, no preflight, no `[hooks]`, no `[publish] commands` — and **no plugin dispatch
at all**, not even `on_pre_bump`, which `bump --dry-run` still dispatches. That is what makes it safe on
a dirty tree and on a branch that is not `main`, which is where a CI job needs to plan.

The plan is derived, not described: the same code that runs the bump produces it, so a `plan` that
disagrees with a `bump` is a defect with one place to look. Blockers are data — a dirty tree, a
mismatched `require_branch`, an existing release tag — and a blocked plan still exits 0, because a plan
you can read is the point. Exit 1 means it could not compute one.

## `cutver attest`: a gate's verdict as a fact
[#331](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/331) · `[gates]` in `cutver.toml`

```bash
cutver attest ci --commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" --conclusion success --run "$RUN_URL"
```

A gate is a name, a commit, a conclusion and the day it was recorded, written as one JSON object under
`[gates] dir` (default `.cutver/attestations`). `publish` then requires every gate named by
`[gates] require` plus every `--require-gate` on the invocation, deduplicated, and refuses a missing
attestation or a recorded failure before the tag exists. "This was verified" stopped being a sentence in
a workflow and became something the tool can refuse on.

Declared artifacts carry the other half ([#330](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/330)): the files a
release promises are downloaded and their digests verified **before** the tag is created, so a release
that cannot produce its assets never gets a tag to begin with.

## The CI channel: the tool writes what the workflow used to parse
[#332](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/332)

Detection is `GITHUB_ACTIONS` true plus a writable `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` or `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, and the
channel is on by default when detected. `--ci` and `--no-ci` are global flags, so a runner can always
turn it off — a flag that silently does nothing is the defect this release is trying to remove.

- `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` gets the field names the machine payload already carries, one `key=value` per line:
  `released`, `deferred`, `version`, `tag`, `commit` for `bump`; `next_version`, `tag`, `commit` for
  `plan`. A value the run does not have is omitted rather than written empty, which is why a `--dry-run`
  bump writes no `commit` line.
- `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` gets one bounded markdown block per run. Text that originates in your content —
  a changelog entry, a commit subject — is escaped or fenced, so it cannot inject structure.
- On failure, one `::error::` line goes to **stderr** carrying the same text as the human error. Nothing
  is ever added to stdout, so the machine contract ("stdout is the payload") stays literally true.

This repository's own `release.yml` now reads those outputs instead of parsing a JSON report with `jq`
([#342](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/342)), which is what the channel was for.

## Release notes: a stream, and sections for templates
[#310](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/310) · [#311](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/311)

`cutver publish --notes-file -` reads the notes from standard input, and an empty stream fails closed
with `release notes on stdin were empty` before the tag, the pushes or the publish commands run. A
streamed run declares no path in the worktree, so a transient notes file stops being something the
clean-tree guard has to know about.

Custom note templates now receive `sections` in the release context: an ordered sequence of
`{heading, entries, is_breaking}`, resolved once by the host. A breaking entry appears in the breaking
section only, empty sections are omitted, and a release with no commits yields an empty sequence rather
than a template that renders nonsense.

## Fixes

- **Hooks are bounded, with a tree kill** ([#314](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/314)): both hook
  kinds share the supervised spawn that preflight already used, so a hook that outlives its timeout no
  longer leaves descendants holding the pipes.
- **The tag prefix is read where it is written** ([#312](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/312),
  [#313](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/313)): `changelog` reads existing headings through the
  configured prefix, and `doctor` lists changelog versions through it too.
- **The install action verifies what it installs** ([#325](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/325)):
  `cutver/setup` checks the `SHA256SUMS` of the release before extracting and fails closed, pinned by
  commit.

## What this release does not include

- Phases 5 and 6 of [#326](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/issues/326): `--channel` with promotion and
  `publish --resume`, and declared per-phase needs with `--root`. The CI contract is complete through
  phase 4; those two phases are open.
- The attestation section on the two integration pages. `cutver attest` and `--require-gate` are
  documented in the [CLI reference](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/blob/main/docs/reference/cli.md);
  the end-to-end flow on the GitHub Actions pages is still missing and tracked.
- This release was cut by the pipeline it describes, and that is the only place its own workflow was
  exercised for real: no test can execute a workflow. The dry-run dispatch proved the branch where
  nothing publishes; this one proves the branch where everything does.
